name: k-Core Decomposition
problem_statement: Assign every vertex its largest k for which it belongs to the maximal induced subgraph whose vertices all have internal degree at least k.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Collapse parallel edges into one undirected edge.

problem_inputs.name: requested_k
problem_inputs.description: Optionally materialize the vertices and edges of one k-core in addition to the full decomposition.

required_outputs.name: core_number_by_vertex
required_outputs.description: Largest core order containing each vertex.

required_outputs.name: degeneracy
required_outputs.description: Maximum core number in the graph.

optional_outputs.name: requested_core_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Vertices whose core number is at least requested_k.

optional_outputs.name: peeling_order
optional_outputs.description: A valid order in which vertices were removed.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the complete core decomposition and graph degeneracy.
solution_semantics.exactness: Core numbers and degeneracy are exact.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each input vertex has exactly one core number.
solution_semantics.ordering: Peeling order may vary while core numbers remain invariant.

validation_rules: Every vertex assigned core c belongs to the c-core.
No vertex belongs to a core with order greater than its reported core number.
The requested k-core equals vertices with core number at least k.
edge_cases: Isolated vertices have core number zero.
An empty graph has degeneracy zero and an empty map.
Every vertex in a complete n-vertex graph has core number n-1.
